 ORDER

The appellants filed this appeal against the respondents under Sec.9(1) of the Public Premises (Eviction of Unauthorised Occupants) Act, 1977, with prayer to set aside the order dated 05.05.2022 in Estate Case No.B/W-274 ENCRO ON RLY LAND AT Hosur, Bengaluru, passed by the 2 nd respondent, directing the appellants to vacate the premises within 14 days and prayed to allow the appeal.

sentences.text: 2. Case of the appellants in brief is that, the Estate Officer / respondent No.2 initiated proceedings under the Public Premises (Eviction of Unauthorized Occupants) Act, 1971 against the appellants and others by issuing a notice under Sub-Section (1) of Section 5 alleging that, the appellants have encroached upon the railway property to the extent of 280.35 sq. mtrs. and constructed (G+2) floor building at Benniganahalli.

entities.text: Public Premises (Eviction of Unauthorized Occupants) Act, 1971
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The appellants were called upon to respond to all material questions and present evidence before the Estate Officer on a specified date.

3. In response to the notice, the appellants appeared before the Estate Officer and filed objections and produced relevant documents including sale deeds, katha extracts and building sanction plan issued by the BBMP.

4. The Estate Officer by impugned order, allowed the claim of the South Western Railway,
Bengaluru i.e., respondent No.1 and directed the appellants and others to vacate the encroached Nagappa R Since Dead By Lrs Gowramma vs The Divisional Railway Manager on 9 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/63456677/
2 portion of the land within the stipulated period.

sentences.text: 5. Aggrieved by the impugned order, the appellants have preferred the present appeal contending that, the Estate Officer failed to appreciate the facts, particularly, regarding the appellants' title over the disputed land, which they acquired under the partition / gift deeds dated 20.12.2019 from their father.
The appellants further contended that, they are in possession and enjoyment of the property by paying taxes to the BBMP.

They claimed that, their grandfather Ramaiah S/o. Devanna purchased property measuring 19 guntas in Sy.No.4 of Benniganahalli Village under the registered sale deed dated 11.08.1971 from B.S.Krishnamurthy S/o. Late Kantappa and pleaded about flow of title to the property.
After obtaining necessary permission from the BBMP, building has been constructed.
The appellants contended that, the Estate Officer / respondent No.2 failed to consider the objections properly and erred in passing the impugned order.

6. In the year 1991, when the Estate Officer issued similar notice to Nagappa, he filed W.P.No.19283/1991, wherein, the Hon'ble High Court directed the respondents to consider the objections and to pass suitable order.
Thereafter, for a period of 25 years, the respondents have kept quite and now they have initiated the present proceedings.
Hence, the appellants have perfected their title to the property by way of adverse possession as they are in unobstructed possession and enjoyment of the property for a period more than 12 years.
Therefore, the appellants prayed to set aside the impugned order by allowing this appeal.

7. The respondents filed detailed objections to the appeal contending that, the land to the extent of 1 acre 13 guntas in Sy.No.4 of Benniganahalli Village was notified for formation of Bengaluru to Salem Railway Line Project in the year 1962.

During inspection by railway authorities, determined the actual encroachment on the railway property in Sy.Nos.4 & 5 and found that, the property in appellants' possession was within the Sy.No.4 of Benniganahalli Village and was encroached upon.
The respondents asserted that, the appellants unauthorisedly constructed the building.

Therefore,
the Estate Officer / respondent No.2 issued notice under Sec.4(1) of the Act and after following due procedure, passed the impugned order.
Further, it is contended that, appellants have not made out grounds to interfere with the impugned order, hence, prayed to dismiss the appeal.
8. Case record was summoned from the office of the Estate Officer and reviewed.
Heard arguments and perused the entire materials on record.

Now, the points that arise for my consideration are as follows:
1. Whether the appellants have established any grounds to interfere with the impugned order exercising the power conferred under Section 9(1) of the Public Premises (Eviction of Unauthorized Occupants) Act, 1971 ?
2. What order ?
9. My findings on the above points are as under :-
 Point No.1 : In the Negative,

 REASONS  10. POINT NO.1:

sentences.text: , the Court's power to scrutinize the order passed by the authorized officer under Section 5 of the Act, is limited.

Unless, it is found from the fact of the record and order that, the order is perverse or passed without applying the mind by ignoring due procedure and principles of natural justice, the Court refrains from interfering.
11. The special enactment aims to protect public property from land grabbers.
In this context, the facts of the present case must be appreciated before recording any findings on the legality of the impugned order.
According to the respondents, an extent of 1 acre 13  guntas of land in Sy.No.4 of Benniganahalli Village was notified for the Railway Project in 1962.

The appellants claimed to be in possession and enjoyment of the property consisting of two sites of 40 x 60 feet, on which construction has been made and it is divided among the children of Nagappa under the gift deeds dated 20.12.2019.
As per the case of the appellants, their predecessor Ramaiah purchased 19 guntas of land in Sy.No.4 of Benniganahalli Village on 11.08.1971.
Thereafter, Nagappa S/o. Ramaiah put up construction and divided among his children by way of gift deeds.

Hence,it is clear that, the sale deed in favour of Ramaiah, subsequent division and git deeds in favour of appellants are subject to the notification of the 1962, notifying of the land in Sy.No.4 for the Railway.
12. The appellants have contended that, BBMP sanctioned plan for construction of building on the disputed land and they are paying taxes to the BBMP.

As argued by the learned counsel for the respondents, when there is a bar under any special statute to own or construct any building in a notified area or land, merely because the local authority issued no objection certificate or sanctioned the construction plan, it would not confer any right to claim lawful possession over such property.
In this context, it is relevant to refer to the circulars / notifications issued by the Central Government to protect public property.

The Government of India - Ministry of Railway issued a notification dated 25.06.2015, prescribing procedures for issuing No Objection Certificates for construction /
redevelopment of Government and private buildings on land adjoining Railway boundaries.
As per the circular / notification, the Railway's NOC is required for construction within 30 meters from the Railway boundary, as per para 827 of IRWM.
Therefore, no authority can grant permission to construct within the buffer zone or boundary of Railway tracks.

13. The respondents produced a re-survey joint sketch and report prepared by the ADLR dated 03.09.2021, which shows that, the appellants' construction was within the acquired land and prohibited boundary.
The appellants produced photographs showing that, the building extended to the border of the Railway track.

It is well-settled law, as held by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in Bombay Swadeshi Stores Vs. State Bank of Mysore, reported in ILR 1989 KAR 2506,
that, the primary considerations for the authority and the appellate authority in cases of public Nagappa R Since Dead By Lrs Gowramma vs The Divisional Railway Manager on 9 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/63456677/
4 premises encroachment are, whether the premises are public and whether the occupant is unauthorized.

sentences.text: If these questions are answered affirmatively, no further consideration is required.
The records indicate that, the Estate Officer issued notice before initiating proceedings.
The appellants duly appeared and presented documents and the Estate Officer passed the impugned order after considering all contentions.

14. Although, the appellants have set up title regarding the land they allegedly encroached upon, the argument that, title disputes cannot be decided by the Estate Officer in summary proceedings is persuasive.
However, allowing such a defence could undermine the purpose of the special statute designed to protect public property.
Allowing parties to claim title to delay proceedings would defeat the statute's objective.
Even if a local authority issued a sanction plan contrary to the statute, it would not confer any rights to an unauthorized occupant.

Moreover, as the sale deed / gift deeds relied upon by the appellants are subsequent to the Government's acquisition for Railway project,
they cannot claim to protect their possession based on such documents.
15. The appellants contend that, BMRCL awarded compensation in favour of Nagappa on 24.01.2019.
The land in question and the land acquired by BMRCL are different.

As per the joint survey conducted by ADLR and other authorities, the land in dispute where the house of the appellants situated comes within the property belongs to the Railway Department, hence, awarding compensation by BMRCL to some property near to disputed property is not a ground to hold that,
the land in dispute belongs to the appellants.

16. Further, the appellants contend that, after the order of the Hon'ble High Court in W.P.No.19283/1991, the respondents kept quite for a long period, hence, the appellants have perfected their title to the property in dispute by way of adverse possession as they are in continuous possession and enjoyment of the property for more than 12 years.
To claim adverse possession, the appellants have to admit the property belongs to the respondents.
If the appellants admit that, the property belongs to the respondents, then admittedly, from the year 1991, the respondents are taking steps to recover land in dispute.
Further, to claim adverse possession against the Government property, continuous possession of 12 years is not sufficient.
The survey conducted on 03.09.2021 by the government authorities is presumed to be known to the appellants since the survey is conducted in respect of disputed land.
Hence, the appellants cannot plead ignorance about the said survey.
Looking from any angle, this Court do not find any good grounds to interfere with the impugned order as there is no merit in the appeal.
Accordingly, I answer point No.1 is in the Negative.
17. POINT NO.2:-

For the aforementioned discussions, I proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER
The appeal filed by the appellants under Section 9(1) of the Public Premises (Eviction of Unauthorized Occupants) Act 1977, is dismissed with cost.
